basis: Mitochondrial depletion with axonal degeneration; weakness and wasting in 1/1 can be neurogenic. Direct myopathy, pulmonary injury and attributable blood disease are unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: wasting and weakness accompany axonal degeneration; scoliosis in one reported patient does not establish common direct skeletal or muscle damage.

basis: Lipomatous tethering directly affects spinal cord and roots. Neurogenic sphincter deficits do not establish direct bowel/bladder injury; qualifying skeletal involvement is uncertain.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder dysfunction reflects cord/root injury; direct urinary tract damage in >=30% is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: bowel dysfunction is neurogenic; direct intestinal injury in >=30% is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: foot deformities are described, but common direct skeletal disease rather than consequences of neurologic dysfunction is unestablished.

basis: Developmental disability and persistent fetal hemoglobin define the syndrome. Strabismus causes ocular dysfunction in 8/8; hypermobility in 7/8 lacks documented joint damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility in 7/8 establishes laxity, but associated instability, injury or functional loss is not documented.

basis: Combined immunodeficiency with defining autoimmune cytopenias; hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia and aphthous mucosal ulceration each occur in 2/4. Bronchiectasis occurs in only 1/5.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: aphthous ulcers in 2/4 constitute direct oral mucosal injury associated with the immune disorder, rather than an isolated transient inflammatory sign.

basis: Puumala infection causes the defining renal and thrombocytopenic hemorrhagic syndrome; thrombocytopenia occurs in roughly 70-90%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic dysfunction are defining features of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome; thrombocytopenia occurs in roughly 70-90%.

basis: Nasal skeletal hypoplasia and epiphyseal stippling define embryopathy; intellectual disability occurs in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish direct airway or lung injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79%, but direct airway or lung damage is unestablished; nasal bone hypoplasia is a skeletal defect.

basis: Endothelial vascular neoplasm commonly occupies skin/subcutis (>50%) and skeletal muscle/bone (~40% or more); occupation directly damages these tissues.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: dermal/subcutaneous tumor occupation occurs in more than half of patients and represents direct tissue involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle involvement occurs in roughly 40%, with additional bone lesions; direct tumor occupation exceeds the 30% threshold.

basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; hearing impairment occurs in 1/3 (~33%). Muscle atrophy in 3/5 can be secondary to neurologic disability; intrinsic muscle or lung disease is unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy in 3/5 accompanies severe spastic neurologic disability; direct myopathy rather than secondary denervation or disuse is not established.

basis: Loss of coordinated ocular movement defines the disorder and localizes dysfunction to central neural gaze-control pathways.

decisions.neurologic: primary: conjugate gaze palsy intrinsically reflects dysfunction of central gaze-control pathways, regardless of the separately diagnosed underlying cause.

basis: Skeletal ciliopathy; nephronophthisis/CKD and hepatic fibrosis each affect roughly >=30% of reported cases. Retinal frequency is uncertain; thoracic restriction is secondary to skeletal disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: thoracic skeletal hypoplasia causes restrictive breathing; common direct airway or pulmonary parenchymal disease is not established.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal degeneration has no supplied frequency; nyctalopia is occasional (5-29%), leaving >=30% direct ocular involvement unestablished.
